findings.address: scripts/sovrecurrence/declaration.py identity_names() key filter and structural_names() walk; scripts/sovrecurrence/fixture.py _mispaired
findings.claim_defeated: That the exclusion of instance data and the root-only identity rule now have refusal cases wherever the loosening could sit - the two directions this delta closed were the ones that were open.
findings.observed: Three further loosenings pass selfcheck at exit 0, pass all 35 unit tests, and leave the live run byte-identical at 9 of 10 resolved, while genuinely flipping declares() from False to True. L1: relax the identity key filter from key.endswith('_id') to key.endswith('id'), so a root-level bare 'id' key is read. {'$id': unrelated, 'id': 'settlement-v1'} goes False -> True. A bare 'id' at the root is one of the commonest shapes in JSON there is. L2: drop the key filter entirely and collect every whitespace-free root string value. {'$id': unrelated, 'kind': 'settlement-record'} goes False -> True; the whitespace guard alone is what keeps prose out, and nothing in the fixture requires a key-name filter to exist at all. L6: when descending a DECLARED_NAME_KEYS dict, also harvest the keys of each declared name's own dict value, one level deeper. {'properties': {'row': {'settlement_id': {...}}}} goes False -> True. That last one is the near sibling of what this delta did add: the fixture's `sections` block refuses ordinary-dict-key harvesting at the document root, and nothing refuses it one level inside a `properties` subtree, which is precisely the asymmetry P9-F6 named for the instance keys and the delta closed for the instance keys only. Separately, the whitespace guard on root identifiers is caught by test_a_root_identifier_carrying_prose_is_not_an_identifier and not by the self-check; passes 7 and 8 both name that one, it is unchanged, and I am not counting it as new.
findings.why_it_matters: Not a false green: the live reading still reads 9 of 10 and still refuses P15-Q4.3 under all three. It matters because of what the pattern says about the method. Every round on this branch has closed the directions the previous round named and left the neighbouring ones, and this round closed two and left three that are one fixture key away each. The fixture is a list of directions somebody thought of, and the module's docstring calls the surviving rule 'deliberately small' as though smallness were self-certifying. AGENTS.md requires a case proving the required refusal for every consequential behaviour; the identity key filter and the second-level declared-name restriction are consequential behaviours with no refusal case anywhere.

findings.claim_defeated: The commit's own subject line, 'make the candidate identity a function of the artifact', in the injective direction: distinct artifacts must have distinct identities.
findings.observed: The rolling hash concatenates each file's relative path bytes and then its content bytes with no delimiter and no length framing, so the boundary between a path and its content is not recoverable and two different trees collide. Demonstrated: a directory holding one file named `ab` with empty contents, and a directory holding one file named `a` whose contents are the single byte `b`, both digest to fb8e20fc2e4c3f248c60c39b... - identical. The same construction extends to any pair of trees whose concatenated path-and-content streams agree. This is not introduced by the delta and the exclusion repair neither causes nor worsens it.
findings.why_it_matters: It is the other half of the property this commit exists to establish, and the commit now states that property in contracts/custodies/phase-1-5.json without qualifying it. The identity is stable across checkouts, which is what P9-F5 asked for and what the delta delivered; it is not injective over trees, so two different states of a settled member can share one candidate id. Nothing in this repository currently exhibits the collision and it needs adversarially chosen filenames, which is why this is MINOR and not a dissent. It is worth a fixture case because the member's whole claim is that a candidate cites a basis by digest, and a digest that two bases can share is a weaker citation than the note implies.

q1_landing_at_built.question: Does anything at 964abd7 make landing the member at BUILT wrong?
q1_landing_at_built.answer: NO. I do not object to landing.
q1_landing_at_built.reasoning: Five things would make it wrong and none of them is present. A standing the member does not hold: the member reads standing BUILT, work_state PRESENTED, stage_observed_by null, and the note's closing sentence says 'BUILT only. A test may not claim WITNESSED, and this reader cannot cite itself until an independent participant observes it and it lands.' Nothing in the delta claims otherwise and no record in the delta supports a transition. A regression: origin/main is an ancestor of 964abd7, verifies at exit 0 with 55 checks, and the branch verifies at exit 0 with 57 in two separate fresh clones; no check is lost and the module is additive. A check that passes when it should not: I sabotaged the exclusion three ways and loosened the reader six ways, and every direction the delta claims to close does go red. A weakened oracle: declaration.py is byte-identical to 3ffa1b5, so the rule under test was not edited to make its own refusal case pass; the fixture was widened and the tests were added to, never relaxed. Anything outside the concern: six files, all inside it, no secrets, no unrelated change, no module over the size ceiling, no vocabulary drift - standing, work_state and effect-class terms all match CLASSIFICATION.md and SPEC.md usage. On top of that the delta repairs the one defect on this branch that was about what the reader computes rather than what it says, and I confirmed the repair causally against a pre-repair control, not by reading the claim. Landing at BUILT is landing a member that is honest about being unwitnessed. My ten findings are all repairable inside the concern at effect class RECORD_LOCAL and none of them is a reason to hold the branch; P10-F1 and P10-F5 are the two worth doing before anyone proposes WITNESSED, and neither is a reason to refuse a landing.
q1_landing_at_built.what_this_answer_is_not: It is not a witness of the member, not an acceptance, and not a settlement. It says the branch is fit to land with the member at the standing the member itself declares.

objection_to_landing_at_built: NONE. I do not object to landing 964abd7 with custody:phase-1-5/definition-recurrence at standing BUILT, work_state PRESENTED. This is not a witness of the member and grants it nothing.

verdict: REPRODUCED with dissent on three sentences and no dissent on any command claim or code repair. All four delta claims reproduce, two of them - the identity repair and the two closed loosening directions - confirmed causally against pre-repair controls and re-planted attacks rather than read off the prose. I dissent from 'every prose value in the variant is a string' in contracts/custodies/phase-1-5.json and in the commit message, from the retained 'No session, transcript or environment is consulted' which the same paragraph contradicts, and from C7's hybrid quotation in pass4.json. Ten findings, all MINOR or TRIVIAL, all repairable inside the concern at effect class RECORD_LOCAL. Three of them - P10-F1, P10-F4, P10-F5 - are named by no prior reading and are the ones worth the builder's attention; the other seven are wording and placement.
standing_supported: NONE. This observation supports no standing transition. The member stays BUILT at work_state PRESENTED, and the refusal of BUILT -> WITNESSED recorded by passes 1 through 9 is untouched by this reading and was not reopened by it, as directed. This record supports landing the branch with the member at that standing, which is a different act, takes no standing and is not an acceptance. Under grant:standing-landing-loop the landing gate needs verify PASS, lint PASS and an observation from a participant that did not build the change; verify and lint pass at 964abd7 in two independent fresh clones, and this record is such an observation to the extent that a reading inside the builder's container and model family can be one, which is a limit I state rather than resolve.
judgement_items: For the root seat, not asked and not blocking: is an exit clause served by an instrument whose non-tracked-byte exclusions are an enumeration maintained by hand in a third place, disagreeing with the repository's own .gitignore, when the repository ships that declaration and the instrument could read it? The code names this as a limit rather than a guarantee, which is honest. Whether honest-and-enumerated is good enough for a Phase 1.5 exit clause is a judgement, and it is the seat's.

For the root seat, not asked and not blocking: ten readings of this member exist and every one of them is the builder's model family in the builder's container. The custody note says plainly that how independent they are is a question the repository cannot settle. At what point does a further pass of this shape stop being evidence and start being repetition? AGENTS.md says model consensus is never authority; nothing says how many same-family readings a BUILT member may accumulate before the count itself becomes misleading to a later reader.
